title: Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District Election, 2026
description: Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District, encompassing southwestern Louisiana including Lafayette and Lake Charles, is holding an election for the U.S. House of Representatives on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Republican Rep. Clay Higgins, first elected in 2016, is seeking re-election amid a tumultuous election cycle in which the U.S. Supreme Court struck down Louisiana's congressional map as an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, prompting Governor Jeff Landry to suspend the May 16 House primaries and the legislature to pass a new map on May 29, 2026. The district is rated 'Solid R' by nonpartisan analysts, and Higgins is the presumptive Republican nominee after facing no primary opposition. Three Democratic challengers — John Day, Tia LeBrun, and Caleb Walker — are competing in a pending Democratic primary to determine who will face Higgins in the general election.
polling_note: No opinion polls specific to Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District were found as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Clay Higgins
candidates.summary: Clay Higgins is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2016. A former St. Landry Parish sheriff and U.S. Army veteran, he has built a reputation as a conservative firebrand with a strong America First agenda. Higgins was unopposed in the Republican primary and will advance to the general election pending the final primary schedule.

candidates.name: John Day
candidates.summary: John Day is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District. A U.S. Navy veteran (1994–1998) and Lake Charles native, Day has worked in insurance, finance, healthcare, and real estate, and is now a professional writer and film producer. He entered the race in February 2026 after a house fire destroyed his family home, pledging to bring a non-career politician's perspective to Congress and to prioritize constituent service over partisan politics.

candidates.name: Tia LeBrun
candidates.summary: Tia LeBrun is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Louisiana's 3rd Congressional District. A French immersion educator and language specialist from Terrebonne Parish, LeBrun is a member of the United Houma Nation and previously ran for this seat in 2022. She is campaigning as an alternative to incumbent Clay Higgins, emphasizing education, coastal protection, and community advocacy.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific polls exist as of June 2026, which limits confidence. However, the race fundamentals overwhelmingly favor the Republican incumbent. The district is rated 'Solid R' by nonpartisan analysts. Incumbent Clay Higgins has held the seat since 2016 and faced no Republican primary opposition. On the Democratic side, three challengers (John Day, Tia LeBrun, and Caleb Walker) are competing in a pending primary with no clear frontrunner, no major fundraising data, and no polling evidence indicating competitiveness. The Supreme Court's invalidation of Louisiana's congressional map and the subsequent May 29, 2026 remap add procedural uncertainty, but nonpartisan analysts continue to rate the district as Solid R under the new map. Given the district's conservative bent, Higgins's incumbency advantage, and a fractured Democratic primary field, the general election is not expected to be competitive. The rating is safe_r, with a win probability of approximately 96% for Republicans.
